title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically-Controlled Knowledge Exposure
claim: A filtered, controlled-scope training corpus and the model trained on it together form a sandbox that opens many research questions.
layout: Single row, left-to-right: corpus, funnel, model, fan-out to four question boxes
description: A left-to-right flow in one row. At the left, a stack of document cards from a web-scale corpus mixes advanced content (an integral, Maxwell's equation, E=mc², a cardiology note) with simple content ("The cat sat on the mat", 4×8=32). A four-segment funnel follows, colored peach, pink, light blue and blue. Its stages are labeled Age-of-Acquisition Pre-Filter, Curriculum-Based Classification, Symbolic Filtering and Frequency Sampling. Only the elementary cards come out, under the heading LittleCurriculum, Kindergarten to Grade 5. They feed a cartoon blue robot holding a book, labeled LittleLearner. Speech bubbles above the robot show in-scope answers (8+6 is 14, Cats are mammals) and one orange out-of-scope answer (ln(0) = −1). Blue arrows fan out from the robot to four boxes: Scaling, Post-training, Educational science, and a dashed "and plenty more to explore!" box. The eye goes first to the robot and the funnel.
caption: LITTLECURRICULUM and LITTLELEARNER provide a pedagogically grounded sandbox for studying model behavior under precise data constraints. LITTLECURRICULUM is an 88B-token pretraining corpus filtered from FineWeb-Edu [1] to only contain elementary school (K–5) data. On it, we train a 5B model: LITTLELEARNER. Together, they form a well-curated sandbox to study scaling, post-training, educational science and more.
abstract: Modern language models are trained on heterogeneous web-scale text corpora. Consequently, studying knowledge and skill acquisition is difficult, as prior exposure to related content is hard to characterize. To address this challenge, we introduce LittleCurriculum, a curated 88B-token pretraining corpus tailored to U.S. elementary school material, explicitly excluding concepts, facts, and vocabulary taught above Grade 5. Training a 5B-parameter LLM from scratch on LittleCurriculum yields LittleLearner, a model with sufficient language competence for open-ended evaluation, yet with clear knowledge and capability boundaries mapped to interpretable curriculum guidelines. We release LittleCurriculum and LittleLearner as a developmentally restricted sandbox to study how models acquire, represent, and use data under a well-defined training scope. We illustrate the sandbox's utility in a first suite of experiments on injecting new knowledge through post-training and in-context learning. These methods let LittleLearner better utilize existing knowledge, but do not raise out-of-scope capabilities. Our findings underscore the value of this controlled environment for future investigations.
